text: Photography is an art form that involves capturing light through a lens to create a visual image. The exposure of a photograph is controlled by two key settings: shutter speed and aperture. The shutter speed refers to the length of time the camera's sensor is exposed to light, while the aperture is the opening in the lens that controls the amount of light that enters. These two elements work together to determine the overall brightness and depth of the image. By adjusting the shutter speed and aperture, photographers can create a wide range of effects, from fast-paced action shots to dramatic landscapes.
